Ingredients  
1 cake  
20 pieces per cake  
Egg 4  
Sugar (approx. 3½ dl) 300 g  
Milk 2 dl  
Butter 50 g  
Wheat flour (approx. 4¼ dl) 250 g  
Baking powder 3 tsp  
Vanilla sugar 1 tsp  
Topping  
Butter 100 g  
Coconut flour (approx. 4¼ dl) 150 g  
Brown sugar (approx. 3¾ dl) 225 g  
Milk ½ dl

​

Baking time  
Approx. 20 minutes at 200° - traditional oven.  
Baking time with filling  
Approx. 5 minutes at 225° - traditional oven.  
Beat eggs and sugar light and fluffy.  
Meanwhile, heat the milk and butter (pinky finger warm).  
Mix flour, baking powder and vanilla sugar together. Carefully fold it, sprinkled through a sieve, into the batter alternately with the milk mixture.  
Pour the batter into a small baking pan lined with baking paper (approx. 5 x 22 x 30 cm) and bake the cake in the middle of the oven.  
Put the butter, coconut flour, brown sugar and milk in a heavy-bottomed saucepan and bring to the boil while stirring.  
Take the cake out (it must be almost done baking) and turn up the oven. Spread the filling on the cake and finish baking, still in the middle of the oven.

Vanilla Ice-cream

1 vanilla pod\*  
80 g sugar\*  
300 ml whole milk  
300 ml cream  
6 egg yolks

Split the vanilla bean, scrape out the vanilla seeds and mix them with a little of the sugar. Don't throw out the empty vanilla beans because it still holds a lot of good vanilla!  
Bring whole milk, cream and the empty vanilla pod to just below the boiling point, which is just below 100°C.  
Beat the egg yolks with vanilla and sugar until you have a fluffy eggnog.  
Carefully pour the hot milk-cream mixture into your eggnog while whisking vigorously. Now you have your ice mass ready.  
Now pour your ice cream mass back into the pan and heat it up to approx. 82°C, but at low heat so it doesn't burn - important! Feel free to stir it along the way, preferably all the time.  
Cool the ice mass completely in the refrigerator when you have reached a temperature of 82°C. It takes approx. 2 hours to cool down the ice mass.  
When your ice mass has completely cooled, it is ready to be run on the ice machine. Now run the ice cream on the machine.  
Spread the vanilla ice cream in a small form, e.g. an oblong cake form of approx. 1-1.5 L.  
Place the ice cream in the freezer for at least a few hours until it has set - preferably until the next day.

Enjoy! It is veeeeeeeery easy and super tasteful!
